correctness.rationale: For n=4pq (p<q distinct odd primes), proper unitary divisors are exactly {1,4,p,q,4p,4q,pq}. Nonempty equal-sum partition exists iff signed sum=0; normalize sign of pq positive. Each independent sign pair gives an element of S={-5,-3,3,5}, reducing to q(p+u)=-(vp+w). For p>=11, p+u>=p-5>0 and q<=5(p+1)/(p-5)<p, contradiction; inequality p^2-10p-5>0 already holds at 11 and increases. Exhaustively evaluating all 64 (u,v,w) for p=3,5,7 gave candidate q sets respectively {5,6,7,9,10}, {6,9,10,11,14,15}, {8,9,10,12,13,15,16,19,20}; zero-denominator cases have no identities. Prime q leave (3,5),(3,7),(5,11),(7,13),(7,19), and explicitly checking both partition sums for 60,84,220,364,532 proves existence. Complete symbolic exclusion handles every larger prime and finite enumeration handles the residual set, not a bounded-only scan.
